name: Rwanda and Uganda: gorillas and chimps

cities.base: Kiyovu or Kimihurura. Both are ten minutes from the airport side of town, walkable at night, and within a short drive of Gisozi for the Memorial.
cities.name: Kigali

cities.base: Kinigi, within fifteen minutes of the park headquarters, because the briefing is at 07:00 and Musanze town adds half an hour in the dark.
cities.name: Volcanoes National Park (Kinigi)

cities.base: Sleep in the sector your permit names. Rushaga in the south is closest coming from Rwanda; Buhoma in the north is the oldest and most comfortable. Buhoma to Rushaga is three to four hours of dirt, so
cities.name: Bwindi Impenetrable Forest

cities.base: The Rutinda side at the north end, where the boats leave and you can walk to a bar. Island lodges are quieter but you are on somebody else's canoe timetable.
cities.name: Lake Bunyonyi

cities.base: Mweya peninsula. The Kazinga boat leaves from below the lodge and the Kasenyi plains are forty minutes east, which is what an early game drive needs.
cities.name: Queen Elizabeth National Park

cities.base: Near Kanyanchu or in the Kasenda crater lakes twenty minutes away. Fort Portal town is forty minutes out and too far for an 08:00 chimp briefing.
cities.name: Kibale Forest and Fort Portal

places.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
places.note: Entry is free; the 30 dollar Ubumuntu package buys the audio guide, which is the version worth doing. Over 250,000 victims are buried in the gardens, no photography is allowed inside, and the children's room at the end will take the rest of your day, so do not book anything after it.

places.name: Campaign Against Genocide Museum
places.note: Inside the old Parliament building, still carrying its shell holes, telling the RPF's military account of how the killing was stopped. It is the state's version of events and reads that way. Confirm the entry fee at the door; published rates vary.

places.name: Kandt House Museum of Natural History
places.note: The first permanent house in Kigali, built for the German colonial resident Richard Kandt, now covering colonial Rwanda and local geology. Small, and the colonial section is more interesting than the snakes in the yard.

places.name: Nyamirambo Women's Center walking tour
places.note: Three hours through the oldest and most Muslim quarter of Kigali with a guide from the co-operative, ending with lunch cooked in someone's house. Book two days ahead; walk-ups are usually turned away.

places.name: Kimironko Market
places.note: The biggest covered market in the city: produce at the front, kitenge fabric and tailors at the back who will run you up a shirt in a day. Prices triple on sight of a foreigner, so agree everything first.

places.name: Question Coffee Cafe
places.note: Sources from a network of women coffee farmers and roasts on site. They run a cupping session if you book it. The best coffee in a city that grows a lot of it and exports almost all of the good stuff.

places.name: Inzora Rooftop Cafe
places.note: Above Ikirezi bookshop, looking over the valley toward Kacyiru. Good for the hour between the Memorial and dinner when you do not want to talk to anyone.

places.name: Repub Lounge
places.note: Rwandan cooking taken seriously: goat brochettes, isombe, ubugali, tilapia from Lake Kivu. Terrace tables over the valley. Service runs slow, so order early.

places.name: Heaven Restaurant
places.note: Open-sided dining under the trees, a hospitality training programme behind it, and the most reliable kitchen in Kigali. It is where every visiting foreigner ends up, which is the cost of that reliability.

places.name: Hotel des Mille Collines poolside
places.note: The hotel where 1,268 people sheltered in 1994 and drank the pool dry. There is no memorial and no plaque, just a working hotel bar. Rwandans are largely uninterested in the film; do not raise it with staff.

places.name: Nyandungu Eco-Park
places.note: A degraded wetland on the eastern edge of the city rebuilt into ten kilometres of boardwalk and path, with around a hundred bird species. Go at opening for the birds and to beat the heat.

places.name: Niyo Arts Gallery
places.note: Painter Niyonsenga Pacifique's gallery, funding an arts school for street children, with a small cafe and a drumming session most afternoons. The hard sell on canvases is real but the work is his own.

places.name: Kinigi park headquarters briefing
places.note: Everyone with a permit is here by 07:00, drinking coffee while Intore dancers perform and rangers sort 96 people into eight groups by fitness. Tell them honestly how fit you are; it decides which family you get and how far you walk.

places.name: Gorilla trek, Volcanoes National Park
places.note: 1,500 dollars for one hour, and it is the single biggest line in the budget. Permits sell out six to twelve months ahead, only 96 go per day, minimum age is 15, and there are no refunds if you are ill on the morning. The walk in is one to four hours of wet nettles and volcanic mud at altitude. Hire

places.name: Golden monkey tracking
places.note: An endangered monkey found only in these volcanoes, tracked in the bamboo zone on flattish ground. A hundred dollars, half a morning, minimum age 12. Photographing them is much harder than photographing gorillas because they never stop moving.

places.name: Dian Fossey tomb hike
places.note: Three hours up to the Karisoke site at 3,000 metres, where Fossey lies beside Digit and the other gorillas she buried. The camp itself is gone. Steep, slippery and cold, and most people find it heavier going than the gorilla trek.

places.name: Mount Bisoke summit
places.note: 3,711 metres with a crater lake in the top, up and down in one hard day, 1,200 metres of gain. The final section is a mud staircase. Do not put this next to a trekking day.

places.name: Ellen DeGeneres Campus, Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund
places.note: The Fossey Fund's research base, opened in 2022, with an exhibition on Karisoke and fifty years of daily gorilla monitoring. The building is worth the visit on its own. Tour prices have moved more than once; confirm before you go.

places.name: Musanze Caves
places.note: Two kilometres of lava tube used as a refuge and, in 1994, as a killing site. Walkways and helmets are provided. Bats, cold air and a lot of guano. A decent filler on an afternoon you cannot spend in the park.

places.name: Buhanga Eco-Park
places.note: A small sacred forest where Rwandan kings were crowned, with fig trees over a lava floor. Quiet and quick. Forty dollars is steep for ninety minutes, so skip it if the budget is tight.

places.name: Twin Lakes Burera and Ruhondo
places.note: Two crater lakes an hour east of Musanze with the volcano chain behind them, and dugout canoes for hire from the shore. Clear mornings give the view; by mid afternoon the volcanoes are usually in cloud.

places.name: Gorilla Guardians Village
places.note: A reconstructed village staffed by reformed poachers, doing dancing, archery and a mock king. The money genuinely goes to the community but the performance is staged flat, and the Nyamirambo walk in Kigali does the same job honestly.

places.name: Volcana Lounge
places.note: The town restaurant in Musanze: wood-fired pizza, brochettes, cold Mutzig. Where guides eat on their night off. Half the price of the lodge dining room and better company.

places.name: Bisate Lodge dining room
places.note: Thatched pods built into an eroded volcanic cone facing Bisoke and Karisimbi, with a kitchen that outclasses anything for a hundred kilometres. Non-resident lunch is possible if you book, but they prioritise house guests.

places.name: Gorilla trek, Rushaga sector
places.note: The same species for 800 dollars instead of Rwanda's 1,500, dropping to 600 in April, May and November. Rushaga has the most habituated families in Bwindi. Permits still sell out six months out and discounted ones cannot be moved. You get one hour after up to six of climbing through vines.

places.name: Gorilla habituation experience, Rushaga
places.note: Four hours with a semi-habituated family alongside the researchers, and the only place in either country it is offered. Four permits a day, so book a year out. The gorillas are twitchier and the day is twice as long, which is the trade for the extra three hours.

places.name: Gorilla trek, Ruhija sector
places.note: The high eastern sector at 2,350 metres, home to Bitukura, Oruzogo and Kyaguliro. Coldest and quietest of the four, often in cloud all morning. Bitukura is usually the shortest walk in Bwindi when it stays near the road.

places.name: Gorilla trek, Buhoma sector
places.note: Where Ugandan gorilla tourism started in 1993, with Mubare and Rushegura. Lowest elevation in the park and usually the easiest walk, which is why these permits go first. Buhoma is a four-hour drive from Rushaga, so do not book them back to back.

places.name: Gorilla trek, Nkuringo sector
places.note: The hardest sector. You start on a ridge at 2,100 metres and descend six hundred metres into the forest, which means you finish by climbing all of that back out. Take a porter here. The views across to the Virungas are the best in Bwindi.

places.name: Munyanga River Trail
places.note: A short self-guided loop from the Buhoma gate along the river, good for turacos and the occasional gorilla that wanders down. The one thing you can do in Bwindi on an afternoon without paying for anything.

places.name: Buhoma waterfall trail
places.note: Three hours through the forest to three waterfalls, with a ranger, past tree ferns and epiphytic orchids. Slippery throughout and a real sense of why the place is called impenetrable.

places.name: Mubwindi Swamp trail
places.note: The five-hour walk birders come to Bwindi for, down to the swamp where the African green broadbill is found. Steep going back up. Bring a scope or go with someone who has one.

places.name: Batwa cultural experience, Buhoma
places.note: The Batwa were evicted from this forest in 1991 when it became a national park and were given no land and no share of the permit money. The demonstration of hunting and fire-making is staged, but the account of what happened to them is not, and it is the necessary counterweight to the 800 dollars yo

places.name: Ride 4 a Woman
places.note: A women's co-operative in Buhoma running sewing, basketry and a guesthouse, started around bicycle hire. You can sit at a treadle machine and make a bag badly. Prices are fixed and fair.

places.name: The Bwindi Bar
places.note: A training bar run for young people from the villages around the park, doing coffee, cake and cold beer on the Buhoma strip. The only place in the sector where you are not eating at your own lodge.

places.name: Bwindi Lodge dining room
places.note: Volcanoes Safaris' camp right on the forest edge, where gorillas from the Rushegura group cross the lawn often enough that it is not a sales line. Book non-resident meals ahead; the kitchen cooks to guest numbers.

places.name: Punishment Island (Akampene)
places.note: A few square metres and one tree, where the Bakiga left unmarried pregnant girls to starve or drown until the practice ended in the 1940s. Some were taken off by men too poor to afford a bride price. Go with a local paddler who will tell it straight, not with a motorboat.

places.name: Arcadia Lodge viewpoint
places.note: The highest terrace over the lake, looking down on twenty-odd islands and the terraced hills behind them. Buy a drink and stay for sunset. The access road is rough and steep; do not attempt it in a saloon car.

places.name: Bushara Island
places.note: A conservation-run island camp fifteen minutes off Rutinda, with a short nature trail, a swimming platform and good cake. Day visitors are welcome. The eucalyptus and pine were planted; the birds came anyway.

places.name: Byoona Amagara, Itambira Island
places.note: Open-sided geodomes on an island at the south end, backpacker prices and a kitchen that does crayfish from the lake. Forty minutes by dugout, fifteen by motor. Solar power only, so charge everything first.

places.name: Swimming off BirdNest Resort
places.note: Bunyonyi has no bilharzia, no hippo and no crocodile, which makes it the only water on this trip you can get into. It sits at 1,960 metres, so it is cold. The jetty here is the easiest entry on the north shore.

places.name: Rutinda landing and market
places.note: Where the boats load and the shore trade happens: sweet potato, crayfish, a lot of waiting. The big market runs midweek rather than daily, so ask your lodge which day before you plan around it.

places.name: Bufuka village walk
places.note: Two and a half hours through a Bakiga farming village on the terraces above the water, past a primary school and a sorghum press. Steep the whole way. The guide is from the village and the fee stays there.

places.name: Bunyonyi Overland Resort bar
places.note: The overland truck crowd stops here, so it is the one place on the lake with a crowd and a pool table. Loud by Bunyonyi standards, which means you can hear a conversation.

places.name: Sunrise dugout paddle
places.note: Mist on the water at 06:30 and the hills coming out of it. Hire a dugout with a paddler rather than taking one out yourself; the local canoes go in circles for anyone who has not grown up in one.

places.name: Kabale town
places.note: Seven kilometres from the lake and the last proper supermarket, pharmacy and ATM before Bwindi or Queen Elizabeth. Stop here for cash in Ugandan shillings; the lodges on the lake rarely take cards.

places.name: Kazinga Channel boat launch
places.note: Two hours down the natural channel joining Lake George to Lake Edward, with one of the densest hippo concentrations anywhere and elephant and buffalo on the bank. Thirty dollars for the boat plus a forty dollar park entry valid 24 hours. Take the 16:00 for the light.

places.name: Kasenyi plains game drive
places.note: Out at 06:00 across open grassland where the Uganda kob hold their breeding leks and lions hunt them. Best cat odds in the park. Lion numbers here have dropped badly from poisoning, so no guide can promise you anything.

places.name: Ishasha tree-climbing lions
places.note: The southern sector where lions lie in the branches of the big fig trees, one of only two populations that reliably do it. Two hours south of Mweya on dirt, so do it on the transfer day from Bwindi. Some days the trees are empty and there is no second attempt.

places.name: Kyambura Gorge chimpanzee trek
places.note: A hundred-metre-deep forested canyon cut into the savannah holding an isolated troop of about thirty chimps, cut off from other populations. Around seventy percent success. At a hundred dollars it is the cheap gamble; Kibale at 250 is the one that works.

places.name: Lake Katwe salt works
places.note: Salt has been cut from this crater lake by hand since the sixteenth century and still is, in brine that burns skin. The guides are workers. It is uncomfortable to watch and the most honest hour in the park.

places.name: Katwe explosion crater drive
places.note: Twenty-seven kilometres of track over the rims of a field of explosion craters, with the Rwenzoris to the north when they are out, which is seldom. Flamingos on the salt lakes below. Needs high clearance after rain.

places.name: Baboon Cliff viewpoint
places.note: A rock terrace above Lake Edward and the channel, and the standard sundowner stop. The baboons are habituated and will take food out of your hand and your bag. Keep the car shut.

places.name: Tembo Canteen, Mweya Safari Lodge
places.note: The cheap terrace at Mweya, above the channel, doing burgers and tilapia at half the main dining room price. Warthog graze the lawn in front of it. Non-residents can eat here without booking.

places.name: Kyambura Gorge Lodge dining terrace
places.note: A converted coffee store on a ridge over the gorge with its own kitchen garden and a serious bar. Book ahead if you are not staying. They run a coffee and banana plantation walk from here in the morning.

places.name: Maramagambo Forest walk
places.note: Medium-altitude forest in the south of the park with crater lakes, forest monkeys and a bat cave with a resident python. The bat cave is now viewed from a screened hide after a Marburg outbreak, and that is the right decision.

places.name: Kikorongo equator monument
places.note: Two concrete rings on the Kasese road at latitude zero, with craft stalls around them. Ten minutes and a photograph. The water-draining demonstration is a trick.

places.name: Lion tracking with the research team
places.note: Out with the Uganda Carnivore Program using radio collars, allowed off-road where normal vehicles are not. A hundred dollars on top of park entry and it funds the monitoring. Success is high but you may spend two hours in long grass first.

places.name: Chimpanzee trek at Kanyanchu
places.note: 250 dollars, briefings at 08:00 and 14:00, six people to a ranger, one hour with the chimps. Around 1,500 live in this forest and success runs above ninety percent. Flat walking, but chimps travel fast and you will be half running through undergrowth to keep up. Minimum age 13.

places.name: Chimpanzee habituation experience (CHEX)
places.note: Three hundred dollars buys the whole day with the researchers, from the chimps leaving their night nests at dawn to building new ones at dusk. Twelve hours, most of it waiting. Cheaper per hour than anything else on this trip and the only way to watch chimps behave normally.

places.name: Bigodi Wetland Sanctuary walk
places.note: Community-run boardwalk through Magombe swamp outside the park, with eight primate species including red colobus and grey-cheeked mangabey, and around 200 birds. The fee funds the local school. Wear boots; the boardwalk gives out in places.

places.name: Kasenda crater lakes drive
places.note: Around thirty explosion craters between Kibale and Fort Portal, most now lakes. Lake Nyinambuga is the one on the back of the 20,000 shilling note. Murram tracks, slow going, and the best afternoon in this part of Uganda.

places.name: Top of the World viewpoint
places.note: A hilltop above Kasenda with a hut selling warm beer and a 360 degree view over five or six crater lakes and the Rwenzoris on a clear evening. Ten minutes' walk up from where the car stops.

places.name: Lake Nkuruba
places.note: A community-protected crater ringed by forest with black and white colobus in the trees above the water. Safe to swim, steep path down. The community campsite here has run since the 1990s.

places.name: Amabere ga Nyina Mwiru caves
places.note: Stalactites behind a small waterfall, tied to a Batembuzi legend about a king who cut off his daughter's breasts. The guides tell it well. Combine with the crater viewpoints above the site rather than driving out for the cave alone.

places.name: Kyaninga Lodge lunch terrace
places.note: Hand-cut crater-rim log lodge above Lake Kyaninga, with the Rwenzoris behind it on the rare clear day. Day visitors can eat and use the pool for a fee. The owners fund the Kyaninga Child Development Centre next door.

places.name: The Dutchess
places.note: Wood-fired pizza, real bread and decent coffee in Fort Portal town, run by a Dutch family for years. The place every overlander and researcher in the district eats at. Rooms upstairs if you are stuck.

places.name: Karuzika Royal Palace, Tooro
places.note: The round palace of the Tooro kingdom on the hill above town, rebuilt with Libyan money in 2001. The current Omukama was crowned aged three in 1995. Interior access depends on whether the king is in residence, so it may be grounds only.

places.name: Tinka's Homestead, Bigodi
places.note: Tinka founded the Bigodi wetland project and runs cooking and craft afternoons at his own house: banana beer, a hoe, a meal you help make. Book through KAFRED in Bigodi a day ahead.

places.name: Kanyanchu night forest walk
places.note: Out with a ranger and a torch after dark for pottos, bushbabies, tree hyrax screaming and the occasional civet. Two hours, and half of what you get is sound rather than sight. Book at the visitor centre by afternoon.

outings.why: Briefing at 07:00, drive to a trailhead, then one to four hours uphill through bamboo and nettles at 2,500 to 3,000 metres. You get one hour with the family and then you walk back down. The altitude is what hurts, not the distance.
outings.name: Gorilla trek from Kinigi
outings.season: All year. June to September and December to February are dri
outings.fallback: Golden monkey tracking, half the day and a tenth of the price.

outings.why: The same animal for 800 dollars instead of 1,500. The trade is thicker forest, steeper ground and more mud than Rwanda. Rushaga has the most habituated families in Bwindi, so allocation is easier.
outings.name: Gorilla trek, Rushaga sector
outings.season: All year. Permits drop to 600 dollars in April, May and Nove
outings.fallback: The Buhoma waterfall trail if you are stood down.

outings.why: Four hours with a semi-habituated family instead of one, with researchers rather than a tour group. Only four permits a day and only in Rushaga. It is a full dark-to-dark day and the gorillas are less settled, so it is harder work than a no
outings.name: Gorilla habituation experience, Rushaga

outings.why: The high eastern sector at 2,300 metres, cold and often in cloud. Bitukura and Oruzogo are the families here. Fewer trekkers than Buhoma and a longer drive from anywhere.
outings.name: Gorilla trek, Ruhija sector
outings.fallback: Mubwindi Swamp trail for the African green broadbill.

outings.why: The original sector, tracked since 1993, with Mubare and Rushegura. Lowest elevation in Bwindi and usually the shortest walk, which is why it books out first.
outings.name: Gorilla trek, Buhoma sector
outings.fallback: Munyanga River Trail from the gate.

outings.why: Briefings at 08:00 and 14:00, six to a group, one hour with the chimps. Flat forest walking, nothing like the gorilla climb. Success rate above ninety percent, but chimps move fast and loud and you will be jogging after them.
outings.name: Chimp trek at Kanyanchu, Kibale
outings.fallback: Bigodi swamp walk for red colobus and grey-cheeked mangabey.

outings.why: Meet the researchers at 06:00 at the nest, stay until the chimps build the next one at dusk. Twelve hours in the forest for 300 dollars. Long stretches of nothing, then an hour of screaming.
outings.name: Chimpanzee habituation experience, Kanyanchu
outings.season: Best in the low months, roughly March to May and November to

outings.why: Two hours on a flat-bottomed boat down the 32 km channel between Lake Edward and Lake George. Hippo in the hundreds, buffalo, elephant coming down to drink, and more water birds than you can name. Take the 16:00 departure for the light.
outings.name: The Kazinga Channel launch
outings.fallback: Sundowners at Baboon Cliff over the channel.

outings.why: Out of the gate at 06:00 for lion on the Uganda kob leks. Open grassland, easy viewing, over by breakfast. Lion numbers here have fallen hard and no guide can promise you one.
outings.name: Kasenyi plains morning game drive

outings.why: The southern sector where lions lie in the fig trees. Two hours down from Mweya, and the lions are in the trees or they are not. Worth doing as the transfer day between Bwindi and Mweya rather than as a separate outing.
outings.name: Ishasha fig trees
outings.season: All year, better in the dry months when the grass is short
outings.fallback: Carry on to Mweya and take the boat instead.

outings.why: A 100-metre-deep forested canyon cut into the savannah, holding an isolated troop of about thirty chimps. Around seventy percent success, so it is the cheap gamble, not the sure thing. Do Kibale if you want to actually see chimps.
outings.name: Kyambura Gorge chimp trek
outings.fallback: The gorge rim walk, no permit needed.

outings.why: Three hours up to the old Karisoke site at 3,000 metres, where Fossey is buried beside Digit. Steep, muddy and usually raining. There is nothing left of the camp, which is part of the point.
outings.name: The Dian Fossey tomb hike
outings.season: All year, worst in April and November
outings.fallback: Golden monkey tracking in the bamboo, three hours.

outings.why: 3,711 metres and a crater lake at the top, up and back in a day. The last third is a mud staircase and the summit is in cloud more often than not. Do not stack this on the day before or after a gorilla trek.
outings.name: Mount Bisoke crater
outings.season: June to September and December to February. Unpleasant in th
outings.fallback: Musanze caves and the Twin Lakes.

outings.why: Paddled out to Akampene, the scrap of land where the Bakiga abandoned unmarried pregnant girls until the 1940s. It is one tree and a story, told plainly by someone from the shore. The paddling is the rest of it.
outings.name: Dugout canoe to Punishment Island
outings.fallback: Swim off the jetty. The lake has no bilharzia, hippo or crocodile.

outings.why: More than 250,000 people are buried in the mass graves outside. Two hours inside, the children's room last, and then nothing else planned for the afternoon. Go on arrival day or the day you leave, not squeezed between other things.
outings.name: The Kigali Genocide Memorial morning
outings.season: All year. Closed the morning of 7 April, and open only from
outings.fallback: The Campaign Against Genocide Museum at Parliament.

destination.name: Rwanda and Uganda: gorillas and chimps
destination.pitch: Two countries, two gorilla permits priced almost two to one, and eleven days of long driving between the hours that matter.
destination.caveat: Permits sell out six to twelve months ahead and are not refundable, each trek buys exactly one hour with the gorillas after two to six hours of climbing wet ground and stinging nettles at 2,300 metres, and most of the rest of the eleven days is spent in a vehicle on broken road. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Kigali is clean, safe and easy to walk, but two nights is the whole of it.
because.food: Food is fuel here. Kigali has real restaurants and good coffee; after that it is lodge buffets and grilled tilapia.
because.nature: Two of the four surviving mountain gorilla populations, roughly 1,500 chimpanzees in Kibale, and the Kazinga Channel, where hippo and buffalo stand shoulder to shoulder on the bank.
because.culture: The Kigali Genocide Memorial, the Batwa communities pushed out of Bwindi, and the Tooro kingdom in Fort Portal.
because.adventure: A gorilla trek is a real climb through thick forest with a machete cutting the line ahead of you.
because.relaxation: Only Lake Bunyonyi qualifies. No bilharzia, no hippo, no crocodile, so you can actually swim.
because.exploration: The route crosses a land border, four ecosystems and two currencies, and no two days look alike.
